title: Celestial Anchors — North, Polaris, Sirius, Regulus, Sun, Moon, Saturn and Sagittarius A*
purpose: Clarify what each recurring celestial object/reference actually is, what coordinate role it can play, and how project symbolism may overlay it without confusing physical astronomy with theological office.
master_rule: A named celestial object is not an Axis, North, center or source merely because the project uses it as a symbol. Declare physical object, coordinate frame, epoch and symbolic role separately.

anchors.physical_type: direction/reference family rather than one object
multiple-star system near current north celestial pole
anchors.astronomy: Polaris is currently close to the north celestial pole and is useful for finding true north in the Northern Hemisphere.
anchors.precession: Earth's axis precesses over about 26,000 years, so the role of pole star changes over millennia.
anchors.boundary: Polaris is not eternally the North Star and is not identical with the abstract Axis.

anchors.physical_type: binary star system / brightest star in Earth's night sky by apparent brightness
anchors.astronomy: Sirius is in Canis Major and is not near the north celestial pole.
anchors.project_role: Dog Star / bright signal / recovered March 31 North-Axis association
anchors.boundary: Dog symbolism is cultural/project mapping; no physical Sirius→North identity follows.

anchors.astronomy: Regulus marks part of Leo's prominent sickle and is commonly used as a bright Leo reference.
anchors.boundary: Regulus symbolism does not establish Son/Lion identity or a physical project axis.

anchors.physical_type: G-type star / central mass-energy source of Solar System
anchors.distinction: Physical source of terrestrial sunlight ≠ metaphysical Source.
Moon's reflected light and orbital phases are physical; project follower/proxy meanings are symbolic.

anchors.physical_type: gas giant planet with rings and north-polar atmospheric hexagon
anchors.distinction: Saturn's hexagon is atmospheric flow; Saturn is not physically a cube.

anchors.physical_type: supermassive black hole at the Milky Way's dynamical central region
anchors.astronomy: Sagittarius A* is the approximately four-million-solar-mass black hole at the center of the Milky Way.
anchors.project_role: Galactic-center / Door comparator in August 2026 conversation
anchors.boundary: A black hole is not a portal to Heaven in established astrophysics; 'Door' is project symbolism.

coordinate_contract.rule: Symbolic association never substitutes for angular measurement.

conversation_genealogy: 2026-03-31: North + Sirius/Dog Star + Axis language recovered.
2026-04-17: user corrected Axis as bidirectional relation rather than Father/Son identity.
2026-08-08: Sagittarius A* called Door; Sun/Earth/Moon assigned project roles.
2026-09-09: measurement canon required physical astronomy and symbolic mapping to remain separate.
